title: FancyZones exclude by pressing shift during drag no longer working
author: Chrisch-Tea
summary: A recent FancyZones input-hook change appears to have regressed zone exclusion when Shift is pressed after a drag begins.

status.label: Regression design ready
status.detail: The report distinguishes pre-held Shift from mid-drag Shift and source shows the consumed bare-Shift path updates DraggingState directly.

next_action.label: Design and test Shift state fix
next_action.reason: Validate key state propagation through the drag lifecycle and cover the mid-drag exclusion regression.

judgment.rationale: The reproduction is precise, the reporter says the previous build worked, and the source path around consumed Shift during WindowMouseSnap is narrow enough for focused design.
evidence: On 0.101.2362.0, pressing Shift during a Notepad drag no longer excludes the window from zoning when hold-shift-to-enable-zones is disabled.
Pre-held Shift still works, which narrows the defect to a mid-drag state transition.
FancyZones::OnKeyDown consumes bare Shift while m_windowMouseSnapper exists and calls DraggingState.SetShiftState(true).
DraggingState::SetShiftState updates m_shift and invokes the key-update callback that recomputes drag state.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue focused regression design and tests for Shift press/release propagation during active move-size drag.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones no longer honors exclusion when Shift is introduced mid-drag, while pre-held Shift remains correct.
known_information: Hold Shift to activate zones is disabled, so Shift should suppress zoning.
The reporter used Notepad on Windows 11 build 26200.9106, German Windows, system installation, user/autostart.
Pre-held Shift works; pressing Shift after the drag starts fails.
The issue was not present in the previous build according to the reporter.
There are no assignees, duplicates, or linked fixes on the issue.
inferences: The consumed key path may update press state but not all drag/end paths may observe the updated state at drop time.
A release-state or callback-ordering gap remains possible and should be tested rather than assumed.
issue_context.analysis: The report already supplies the decision-changing timing distinction. Source confirms a special mid-drag Shift path, so a targeted design and UI test plan is appropriate.
